transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I came in because... I just can't seem to stop launching new projects. It's like my brain is in overdrive. I'm coming up with all these work plans, scheduling myself for new certifications, completely upgrading my home network, and even reaching out to old contacts I haven't spoken to in years. It just gets so intense that I completely blow past normal limits. I don't even realize I'm doing it until my wife or my director at work has to step in and tell me to slow down.

How long has this pattern of launching multiple projects and feeling like your brain is in overdrive been going on? Is it something that's been happening for the past few weeks, or has it been like this for much longer?

It's definitely been longer than a few weeks. I'd say... these stretches where I'm just unusually driven, running on very little sleep, and feeling completely overconfident—they've been a part of my life for roughly a year and eight months now. That's about when this whole pattern really started.

During this year and eight months, have you had periods where you felt significantly depressed, down, or hopeless? If so, how often would you say these low periods occur compared to the times when you're in this driven, overconfident state?

Yeah, I definitely have. Um... there are these stretches where I'll just wake up feeling like a failed version of myself. Everything is just... heavy and flat. It gets to the point where even answering my wife’s normal, everyday questions feels like it's just too much. 

As for how often it happens compared to when I'm in overdrive... it feels like they just kind of trade off. I'll be going a hundred miles an hour for a while, and then eventually I just drop into one of these heavy stretches.

When you have one of these heavy, flat stretches where everything feels difficult—how long do those typically last? Are we talking about days, or do they usually go on for at least a couple of weeks or more?

They definitely go on for weeks at a time, sometimes longer. If I look back over this whole year and eight months since this started, um... I'd say those low, withdrawn periods have probably added up to about seven months in total.

During those times when you're feeling overconfident and running on very little sleep with all these projects going—have you ever experienced anything unusual, like hearing voices or seeing things that others couldn't see, or having beliefs that felt absolutely true to you but that other people thought were strange or unrealistic?

Yeah, actually. Um... when I'm in those really driven stretches, you know, barely sleeping and pushing all those huge plans forward... I've had some strange things happen. Like, I'd be in the server room at work, and I'd swear I could hear people making comments about me in the noise of the fans. And... I also started reading into work emails and messages, convinced there were hidden threats in them. It felt completely real to me at the time.

When you're not in one of those high-energy periods or low periods—when you're feeling more normal and balanced—do you still experience those strange things, like hearing comments in background noise or feeling like there are hidden messages in emails?

Yeah, I do. Um... there have been several stretches, sometimes lasting a few weeks at a time, where my mood feels pretty calm—not especially up and not really depressed either. But even during those flat periods, I'd still catch those brief comments when no one was around. And I still firmly believed that my coworkers' status messages on Teams were actually coded warnings directed at me.

When you're feeling calm and balanced—not high and not depressed—and you notice those comments in the background noise or see coded messages in emails, do you still believe they're real and directed at you, or does it feel more like your mind is playing tricks on you?

I still believe they're real. Um... even when I'm not in a big mood swing, I get completely convinced about it. Like, I'll see certain calendar invites, or notice people's Teams status changes, or just overhear brief hallway comments, and I know they are coded warnings. It feels very clear to me that people are building a case to secretly push me out of the company. So, no, it doesn't feel like my mind is playing tricks on me at all.
